Interface Authentication

All Superinterfaces:
AutoCloseable
All Known Subinterfaces:
SinglePassAuthentication
public interface Authentication extends AutoCloseable
Pluggable authentication provider for the Pulsar v5 client (PIP-478).

The core interface carries only lifecycle. The actual credential work lives on opt-in capability interfaces — segregated by transport (Pulsar binary protocol vs HTTP) and by style (single-pass vs multi-round challenge/response) — that an implementation declares only when it supports them:

  • BinaryAuthDataProvider — single-pass credential for the binary protocol
  • HttpAuthHeadersProvider — single-pass credential for HTTP
  • BinaryAuthChallengeHandler — multi-round challenge/response for the binary protocol
  • HttpAuthChallengeHandler — SASL-style multi-round over HTTP
The convenience composite SinglePassAuthentication bundles the common single-pass combination.

All capability methods are asynchronous (CompletableFuture), so credential acquisition never blocks the Netty event loop.

  • Method Details

    • configure

      default void configure(Map<String,String> authParams)
      Configuration step. Called once by the framework AFTER no-arg construction when the plugin was loaded reflectively from authPluginClassName + authParams. NOT called when the plugin was constructed programmatically by the user — that path presumes the instance is already configured. Default: no-op. Implementations override to read their parameters.

      Configuration is intentionally separate from initializeAsync(AuthenticationInitContext): configuration is static plugin-level data (file paths, URLs, scopes); initialization gives the plugin runtime services and may do I/O.

      Parameters:
      authParams - the parsed authentication parameters

    • initializeAsync

      CompletableFuture<Void> initializeAsync(AuthenticationInitContext ctx)
      Initialization step. Called once by the framework with runtime services after configuration. May do I/O; the returned future completes when the implementation is ready to serve credentials. Never throws synchronously: all failures are reported by completing the returned future exceptionally, never by throwing on the calling thread.

      Must not block the calling thread. The framework may call this from an I/O thread — the binary driver initializes on the connection path, which runs on a Netty event loop — and it never waits for the returned future there: the connection's authentication rounds are chained onto it instead. So start any I/O and return promptly, off-loading blocking work to AuthenticationInitContext.blockingExecutor(). Blocking inside this method before returning the future stalls every connection sharing that event loop.

      Called at most once per driver while it succeeds. If the returned future completes exceptionally the framework does not cache the failure: the next connection attempt calls this again, so a transient initialization failure (an unreachable credential endpoint at startup) recovers on reconnect rather than poisoning the plugin for the client's lifetime.

      Parameters:
      ctx - the runtime services context
      Returns:
      a future completing when the plugin is ready

    • capability

      default <T> Optional<T> capability(Class<T> kind)
      Capability factory — the framework's ONLY discovery mechanism. The framework never uses instanceof on a plugin instance; it asks this method for each capability it may drive. An implementation may therefore serve a capability from a separate internal class, or forward a wrapped delegate's capability, rather than implementing it on this type. The default implementation returns this when the plugin implements the requested interface directly, covering the common case with no override.

      Contract: results are STABLE once initializeAsync(AuthenticationInitContext) has completed — the framework may look a capability up once and cache it for the client's lifetime. The framework never queries capabilities before initializeAsync completes; a result returned before initialization is unspecified. One object may serve several capabilities. Capability objects are owned by this plugin and released by close(); the framework never closes them individually. All capability methods must tolerate concurrent invocation (multiple connections authenticate in parallel); only the rounds of a single exchange are serialized by the framework.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the capability type
      Parameters:
      kind - the capability interface to look up
      Returns:
      the capability if supported, otherwise Optional.empty()
